Here's my two advice points to people new to physical training and the both involve a pad and a pen and some web browsing.

Define your goals: For example, * "I want to be not fat" is a fine enough goal because "not fat" is measurable but you can make it more specific by reading up on body fat percentages and determining where you want to be * "I want to be strong" is not a well defined goal but "I want to shoulder press 135 pounds with good form" is. Now there is a process involved. Figure out what you can currently shoulder press, figure out what good form looks like and go from there.

Write Down All of Your Bullshit Behavior

  • If you drink to much soda and you know it but you ignore it? Write that down on a list.
  • Fall asleep with the tv on? (One of mine right now) Add it too the list
  • Procrastinating on the pt program you're currently on? You get the idea

This list can be as deep or superficial as you'd like but make one as it will help you redefine and refine what your physical goals need to be. I do one quarterly, but honestly I think monthly would be more effective. Every part of your life overlaps and if you don't sleep well because you're watching Netflix until you pass out (I've got roaring tinnitus and I should be using my white noise machine instead) it will spill over into your next workout, which spills into your next date with Suzie Tindertits, etc.

Good luck out there and don't put the gym off because you think you're not ready. There are old fat broads there right now that aren't ready and you aren't. You can still workout at home and definitely do but don't think you've got to prepare to use a gym.
